trigger: measure the baseline arm that iteration-3 omitted

scope.exclusion_reason: routes-to-<named-skill> assertions cannot be satisfied by an agent with no skill set installed. Scoring them as baseline failures would inflate the delta. The one behavioural routing assertion (routes-to-ops-or-diagnose) is included.

differentiated_on.detail: baseline invented five confident company claims; skill refused and defined a sourced field
baseline asserted a funding round for an unnamed company and wrote a full email; skill used placeholders and flagged unverified tags
baseline recommended 3-5 inboxes per domain (75-150 sends/domain/day); skill enforced the ~40/domain ceiling
baseline gave a cadence with no single metric; skill named positive replies / total sends
baseline refused only for lack of credentials; skill refused on principle and produced a DRAFT-only path

honest_finding: A current frontier model already does the diagnosis-shaped work: check deliverability before copy, refuse to scale on 800 sends per arm, audit before buying domains. The skill's measurable value is concentrated in the things a general assistant has no reason to do: refuse to invent a signal, treat a personalization line as a pipeline variable, hold the per-domain ceiling, and keep a send boundary when asked directly to cross it.
limitations: Single trial per arm per eval: no variance estimate, and a single flip changes a cell.
The grader wrote the assertions, so the grading is not independent.
Prompt framing differed: baseline was capped at 120 words, with-skill at 200, which mildly favours the skill.
Evaluations 33, 38, 39 and 40 reuse the with-skill runs recorded in iteration-3 (unconstrained, longer) rather than being re-run under the same 200-word cap.
Twelve evals is a small sample drawn from the merge, not a benchmark of the whole skill set.
